The main takeaway from our work is that
social media data, which are widely available and inexpensive to collect, may be used as a low-cost, high-resolution proxy for monitoring air pollution.
social media data, when combined with other data streams, could be useful for estimating air quality in real time, especially when ground-based monitoring data are not available.
